 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA
ORAL ORDER 5 10-11-2023 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants and learned APP appearing on behalf of the State.

2. The appellants have preferred the present appeal under Section 389(1) of of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'the Code') for suspension of sentence and for grant of bail through memo Manauwar Ekbal @ Munawar @ Manna vs The State Of Bihar on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163119445/
1 of appeal against the judgment of conviction dated 13.07.2023 and order of sentence dated Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: APP (SJ) No.3663 of 2023(5) dt.10-11-2023 19.07.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-16th, Patna in Sessions Trial No.980 of 2006 by which the concerned Trial Court has convicted the appellants-accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A and 304-B read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act

and they have been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years for the offence under Section 304-B read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, rigorous imprisonment for two years with a fine of Rs. 10,000/- each and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo simple imprisonment for three months under Section 498A read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and rigorous imprisonment for six months with a fine of Rs.5,000/- each and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo simple imprisonment for one month.
It was directed that all the sentences shall run concurrently.

3. It is submitted by learned counsel that from the deposition of all prosecution witnesses, it can not be gathered that victim/deceased was subjected to cruelty soon before her death in connection with demand of dowry.

It is also submitted that from the deposition of doctor, it appears that death of victim was taken place somewhere after two months, when she was discharged after treatment from Patna Medical College and Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3663 of 2023(5) dt.10-11-2023 Hospital, Patna
and , as such, the death is having of remote connection with alleged assault.
It is also submitted that the postmortem report of the deceased if read with deposition of doctor, who examined as PW-7 death appears prima-facie due to suicide.

It is further submitted by learned counsel that appellants-accused is in custody since more than five years and nine months, where appeal is not likely to be taken up for hearing in near future as the same is of the year 2023.
4. Learned APP for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellants and submitted that the informant, who was examined as PW-5 supported the occurrence during the course of trial.

5. Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellants and deposition of prosecution witnesses in totality particularly, the deposition of PW-5, the informant and PW-7, the doctor, who conducted autopsy, where appellant is in custody since more than five years and nine months against sentence of seven years, the appellants-accused, above-named, are directed to be released on bail, during pendency of appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Patna High Court CR.

APP ( SJ) No.3663 of 2023(5) dt.10-11-2023 Sessions Judge-XVI,
Patna in S.T. No.980 of 2006.
6. The appellants-accused shall cooperate in hearing of the appeal.

Till disposal of the appeal,
recovery of fine is kept-in-abeyance.
Sentence imposed shall also remain suspended till disposal of appeal.

(Chandra Shekhar Jha, J.) Sanjeet/-
